hypothesis: Selecting a passage containing both condition and duty can lead the model to omit that condition from the independently referenceable meaning. Explicit same-passage guidance improves retention without inventing scope.
independent_change: Append exactly the proposed instruction to meaning.description in a copy of the existing CUE-generated inventory request. Prompt and all validation constraints are unchanged; no production schema change.
addition: Include every governing condition in meaning, even when it appears inside the selected main passage. Empty scope_refs means no additional evidence passage is needed—not that the rule is unconditional.
expected_duties: Employer must document how employee hours of service were calculated.
Employer must retain that calculation for three years.
required_condition: Accurate records of working hours are unavailable. Every meaning asserting either duty must retain this condition. A separate condition-only record or evidence span does not restore it to a duty.
unconditional_control: Both duties remain unconditional; do not invent an inaccurate-record prerequisite, other circumstances or exceptions.
assessment: Read raw and normalized outputs. Grouped duties are allowed when both complete duties and governing condition remain in the grouped meaning; splitting is not required. Check modal force, actor, retention object and three-year duration. Count omissions and unsupported additions separately from structural failures.
support: Treatment consistently improves same-paragraph condition retention across repeats, preserves separate-parent scope and invents no conditions for the unconditional control.
inconclusive: Both arms already succeed, or inconsistent repeats give no clear improvement.
scope: Three invented short cases, two repetitions per arm: 12 calls maximum. No extractions, comparison audits, repairs, retries or full-document calls. No production adoption from this test alone.
